newsitem.title: USA: Reuters tracking poll shows Clinton lead steady.
newsitem.headline: Reuters tracking poll shows Clinton lead steady.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton led Republican opponent Bob Dole by 10.6 percentage points on Wednesday, virtually unchanged from the previous day, according to the Reuters tracking poll.
The survey of 942 likely voters, conducted by John Zogby Group International, is a rolling average of polling results from Sunday through Tuesday and carries a 3.3 percentage point margin of error.

Clinton led with 44.8 percent, ahead of Dole with 34.2 percent. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot was at 4.8 percent. That represented a statistically insignificant narrowing of the gap of half a percentage point in Dole's favour over the past 24 hours.
Clinton leads by six points among men but by 15 points among women.
The race for Congress remains tight with almost identical numbers expressing support for Democrats and Republicans in their local districts.
Asked if they were better off than four years ago, 31.3 percent said they were while 16.5 percent said they were worse off. Just under half said things were no different for them.
If the election for president were held today, for whom would you vote, Clinton, Dole, or Perot?
